job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today in science class, we learned that weather is the day-to-day state of the atmosphere, while climate is the average pattern over twenty-five years. I used to think they were the same, but they are quite different. We also discussed how air pressure works; winds actually move from high-pressure areas toward low-pressure regions, which is the opposite of what I previously believed. My teacher explained that the eye of a cyclone is actually a calm, clear area, while the most violent winds and heavy rains occur in the surrounding region. It was fascinating to learn about polar bears too. Their white fur is not for trapping heat, but for camouflage against the snow to help them hunt. I also realized that humidity is always present in the air as water vapor, even on days when it is not raining at all. Finally, we looked at a map and confirmed that penguins live in the South Pole, while polar bears are found only in the North Pole. It is amazing how much I misunderstood about our planet's atmosphere and the animals that live in these extreme environments. I feel much more confident about our upcoming test now.

items.evidence: We also discussed how air pressure works; winds actually move from high-pressure areas toward low-pressure regions, which is the opposite of what I previously believed.
items.q: A region has high air pressure next to a region with low pressure. Which way will wind blow?
options: From the high-pressure area to the low-pressure area
From the low-pressure area to the high-pressure area
From the windy area to the calm area
From the cold area to the warm area
items.explain: Winds move from high-pressure areas toward low-pressure regions, so the air flows out of the high-pressure area.

wrong.why: thinks air moves to fill the low-pressure space the wrong way round
links wind speed with pressure instead of pressure difference
guesses a temperature-based direction not given in the passage

items.evidence: My teacher explained that the eye of a cyclone is actually a calm, clear area, while the most violent winds and heavy rains occur in the surrounding region.
items.q: A cyclone's centre passes over a village. What would people most likely notice there?
options: A short spell of calm, clear sky
The strongest winds of the whole storm
The heaviest rain of the whole storm
A sudden thunderstorm with lightning only
items.explain: The eye is a calm, clear area; the violent winds and heavy rain are in the surrounding region.

wrong.why: thinks the eye is the most violent part
thinks the heaviest rain falls at the centre

items.evidence: Their white fur is not for trapping heat, but for camouflage against the snow to help them hunt.
items.q: Why is a polar bear's white fur useful when it is hunting?
options: It blends in with the snow around
It keeps the bear's body warm
It reflects sunlight into the prey's eyes
It helps the bear float in water
items.explain: The white fur is camouflage against the snow, which helps the bear hunt, not a way to trap heat.

wrong.why: thinks white fur mainly keeps the bear warm
invents a hunting trick not in the passage
guesses another use of fur from everyday ideas

items.evidence: I also realized that humidity is always present in the air as water vapor, even on days when it is not raining at all.
items.q: On a dry, sunny day with no rain, what can we say about humidity?
options: Some water vapour is still in the air
There is no water vapour in the air
It appears only just before rain starts
It is found only near lakes and seas
items.explain: Humidity is always present in the air as water vapour, even when it is not raining.

wrong.why: thinks humidity exists only when it rains
thinks humidity appears only with approaching rain
limits humidity to places near water
